name: Jakob's Law
axiom: Users spend most time on other interfaces, expecting yours to function identically.
trigger: Users hesitate, hunt for navigation, or misuse controls because the layout diverges from conventions they know from other products.

checklist.text: Anchor the logo top-left, global navigation top or left, and account controls top-right.
Keep checkout steps in the expected billing, shipping, and payment order.
Preserve standard keyboard shortcuts and browser history behavior; never hijack them.

antiPattern.violation: A web app rebinds the browser back button to internal tab switching and buries global search in the footer.
antiPattern.remediation: Use declarative HTML5 History entries; keep search in a persistent header input with Cmd/Ctrl+K.

academicOrigin.title: Designing Web Usability: The Practice of Simplicity
